title: SEBI Approves Mahanadi Coalfields IPO as Coal India Sells Ten Percent
excerpt: SEBI has approved the IPO of Coal India's Odisha unit Mahanadi Coalfields, through which the parent will sell a 10 per cent stake, or up to 661.8 million shares.
body:
• India's markets regulator SEBI has approved the initial public offering of Mahanadi Coalfields, a unit of state-run Coal India, in what Reuters described as expected to be one of India's biggest offerings this year.
  • Coal India is selling a 10 per cent stake through the IPO, offering up to 661.8 million shares, according to the draft prospectus cited by Reuters and The Hindu BusinessLine.
  • Mahanadi Coalfields, operating primarily in eastern Odisha, accounted for 21 per cent of India's domestic coal production and 28.4 per cent of Coal India's production in fiscal 2026.
  • For investors: Bloomberg, cited in both reports, said the offering could launch as early as this month, raise as much as $1 billion and value the unit at as much as $10 billion — those are reported estimates, not the IPO's final price or timetable.

India's capital markets regulator has approved the initial public offering of Mahanadi Coalfields, the Odisha-based unit of state-run miner Coal India, according to Reuters. The approval clears the way for what Reuters said is expected to be one of India's biggest offerings this year.

What is being sold

Draft papers filed with the regulator in September showed parent Coal India, the world's largest coal producer, was selling a 10 per cent stake in Mahanadi Coalfields through the unit's IPO, Reuters reported. Coal India is selling up to 661.8 million shares of its unit, the draft prospectus showed. The Hindu BusinessLine carried the same figures in its report of the approval on November 5, 2026.

The structure matters for readers. This is a sale of the parent's existing stake as described in the draft papers, putting a public market price on one of Coal India's largest operating arms rather than describing a new operating business.

Why this subsidiary matters

Mahanadi Coalfields operates primarily in eastern Odisha. It accounted for 21 per cent of India's overall domestic coal production and 28.4 per cent of Coal India's total coal production in fiscal year 2026, according to Reuters. Coal India itself contributed about 74 per cent of India's total coal production in fiscal 2026, so the unit being listed represents more than a fifth of national output inside the group that produces nearly three-quarters of the country's coal.

The longer plan behind the listing

The Mahanadi listing is one step in a broader programme. Coal India had said in March it could sell up to 25 per cent stakes in subsidiaries Mahanadi Coalfields and South Eastern Coalfields through IPOs or other routes, Reuters reported. The Mahanadi draft filing in September was the first concrete filing step described in the reports, and SEBI's approval now moves that specific offering forward.

Bloomberg reported on November 2 that Coal India is preparing to launch the Mahanadi Coalfields IPO as early as this month, citing sources, Reuters added. The offering could raise as much as $1 billion and value Mahanadi Coalfields at as much as $10 billion, that report said. Those figures are Bloomberg's reported estimates as relayed by Reuters and BusinessLine; neither report stated a final issue price, opening date or allotment timetable.

What to watch next

India's capital markets have seen a string of high-profile offerings this year, including those by Jio Platforms and the National Stock Exchange of India, underscoring strong investor appetite for large, marquee listings, Reuters noted. The next facts to watch are the ones not yet in these reports: the final prospectus, the price band and the subscription dates. Until Coal India or the regulator publishes those, diaspora investors interested in applying should treat the $1 billion and $10 billion figures as reported expectations, check the final prospectus on SEBI and the exchanges when it appears, and not act on the approval headline alone.
